Let's introduce the new variable $u={x}^{2}-7.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{9}^{{x}^{2}-7}\,\text{d}x & =\int {9}^{{x}^{2}-7}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {9}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {9}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\frac{{9}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}+C \\  & =\frac{{9}^{{x}^{2}-7}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡9}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=2{x}^{2}-2.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\,{4}^{2{x}^{2}-2}\,\text{d}x & =2\int {4}^{2{x}^{2}-2}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int {4}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {4}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{4}^{u}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =\frac{{4}^{2{x}^{2}-2}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=5{x}^{2}-3.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{10}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\,{5}^{5{x}^{2}-3}\,\text{d}x & =5\int {5}^{5{x}^{2}-3}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int {5}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{10}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {5}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{5}^{u}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C \\  & =\frac{{5}^{5{x}^{2}-3}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=4{x}^{2}-4.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{8}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x\,{7}^{4{x}^{2}-4}\,\text{d}x & =4\int {7}^{4{x}^{2}-4}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\int {7}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{8}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {7}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{7}^{u}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡7}+C \\  & =\frac{{7}^{4{x}^{2}-4}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡7}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=3{x}^{2}-5.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\,{9}^{3{x}^{2}-5}\,\text{d}x & =3\int {9}^{3{x}^{2}-5}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int {9}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {9}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{9}^{u}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡9}+C \\  & =\frac{{9}^{3{x}^{2}-5}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡9}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=2{x}^{2}-6.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\,{11}^{2{x}^{2}-6}\,\text{d}x & =2\int {11}^{2{x}^{2}-6}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int {11}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {11}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{11}^{u}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡11}+C \\  & =\frac{{11}^{2{x}^{2}-6}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡11}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u={x}^{2}-8.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{12}^{{x}^{2}-8}\,\text{d}x & =\int {12}^{{x}^{2}-8}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {12}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {12}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\frac{{12}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡12}+C \\  & =\frac{{12}^{{x}^{2}-8}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡12}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u=1 - 3 x^{4}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=- 12 x^{3}\,⟹\,\left(- \frac{1}{12}\right)\text{d}u=x^{3}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x^{3}\,{6}^{1 - 3 x^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {6}^{1 - 3 x^{4}}\cdot x^{3}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\int {6}^{u}\cdot \left(- \frac{1}{12}\right)\,\text{d}u \\ & =\left(- \frac{1}{12}\right)\int {6}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\left(- \frac{1}{12}\right)\cdot\frac{{6}^{u}}{\ln 6}+C \\ & =- \frac{6^{1 - 3 x^{4}}}{12 \ln{\left(6 \right)}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=- x^{4} - 1.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=- 4 x^{3}\,⟹\,\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)\text{d}u=x^{3}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x^{3}\,{8}^{- x^{4} - 1}\,\text{d}x & =\int {8}^{- x^{4} - 1}\cdot x^{3}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\int {8}^{u}\cdot \left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)\,\text{d}u \\ & =\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)\int {8}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)\cdot\frac{{8}^{u}}{\ln 8}+C \\ & =- \frac{8^{- x^{4} - 1}}{4 \ln{\left(8 \right)}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce the new variable $u={x}^{2}-7.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{3}^{{x}^{2}-7}\,\text{d}x & =\int {3}^{{x}^{2}-7}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {3}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {3}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\frac{{3}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{3}^{{x}^{2}-7}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
